entry.summary: A visa before arrival; e-Visa for tourism, business or medical visits. No visa on arrival.
entry.max_stay: Tourist e-Visas of 30 days, one year or five years; stay limits per visit depend on nationality
entry.pre_arrival: Indian Visa Online only (beware of fakes); print the ETA. e-Arrival Card up to 3 days before travel. An online health self-declaration up to 24 hours before arrival while the Ebola measure lasts.
entry.other: Only some airports accept e-Visas: arriving at one that doesn't means deportation.

tourism.detail: Australians are eligible for 30-day, one-year and five-year e-Tourist options with published stay limits.
tourism.next: Choose the duration on the official portal and keep the visit inside tourist purposes.

meetings.detail: The published purposes include meetings, trade fairs, commercial transactions, venture exploration and company director or partner activity, but exclude petty business and petty trade.
meetings.next: Use the host letter to describe meetings and venture discovery; classify personal stall sales or direct merchandise separately.

conference.route: e-Business e-B5/e-Conference purpose or regular Conference visa with organiser documents
conference.detail: Current official material uses inconsistent labels. The conference option is published for 30 days with multiple entry and needs an invitation plus MEA political clearance; MHA event clearance is added where specifically required.
conference.next: Have the organiser confirm the current portal label and supply the invitation and clearance packet.

unpaid-speaking.route: Conference route or X-Misc for a short non-remunerated cultural appearance
unpaid-speaking.detail: The route follows whether the talk belongs to an approved conference, a cultural event or another exchange.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the organiser and Indian Mission classify the appearance and confirm that no consideration is attached.

paid-speaking.route: Business visa for a remunerated cultural event; Employment visa for qualifying contracted professional service
paid-speaking.detail: India distinguishes a one-off cultural appearance from consulting or service delivery. Employment also requires highly skilled or qualified work and a remuneration test; official documents conflict between ₹16.25 lakh annually, pro-rated, and US$25,000.
paid-speaking.next: Put the fee, contract, event type and duties to the host and Mission and get the current Employment threshold confirmed.

book-launch.route: Business or X-Misc appearance; e-Business for rights and publisher meetings
book-launch.detail: A local publisher or bookseller can handle retail while the author attends for promotion, rights and cultural activity. Petty trade is excluded, so direct author-stall sales are not automatically covered.
book-launch.next: Separate appearance payment, royalties, rights discussions and physical sales; confirm any traveller-handled retail with the Mission.

ai-teaching.route: e-Business for a documented GIAN lecture; Employment visa for qualifying paid teaching or technical service
ai-teaching.detail: The online business route expressly includes GIAN lectures. Other paid teaching must meet the highly-skilled Employment test and a current remuneration threshold that the official documents state inconsistently.
ai-teaching.next: Ask the institution whether it is using GIAN, cultural-event or Employment sponsorship and have the Mission confirm the threshold.

remote-work.detail: The official lists do not publish a remote-worker visa, and tourist and business purposes do not expressly cover routine remote work.
remote-work.next: Map an employment, business-residence or future dedicated route if India becomes a base.

entrepreneur.route: e-Business for exploration and establishment; entity and personal work status mapped separately
entrepreneur.detail: The business route expressly covers establishing a venture and acting as a director or partner.
entrepreneur.next: Choose the company form and sector, then separate ownership, directorship and operational employment.

trade.route: e-Business visa for substantial trade activity
trade.detail: Trade fairs, sourcing, negotiations, supplier assessment and commercial-product transactions fit the published purposes, while petty business and petty trade are excluded.
trade.next: Keep local project execution and installation for a work route, and confirm direct personal retail before selling.

artist.route: Business for a one-off remunerated cultural event; Employment for qualifying regular contracted performance; X-Misc when short and unpaid
artist.detail: The route tracks the contract and remuneration. A regular Employment route also carries the highly-skilled test and disputed current threshold.
artist.next: Have the promoter state the event type and ask the Mission to confirm both visa class and any Employment threshold.

mixed-mission.route: e-Business visa for the business parts
mixed-mission.detail: The e-Business visa covers business activities; employment, journalism or filmmaking need other visas.
mixed-mission.next: Ask the High Commission of India.

volunteering.detail: Smartraveller: contact the nearest Indian embassy or consulate about visa requirements before volunteering.

research.route: Research visa (registration on arrival for long stays)
research.detail: Smartraveller lists research among visa types that must register with the authorities; a tourist e-Visa doesn't cover it.

filming.route: A film or journalist visa, not an e-Business or tourist e-Visa
filming.detail: The e-Business visa isn't valid for journalism or filmmaking.
filming.next: Ask the High Commission of India which film visa fits.

laws.rule: If you're charged with an offence or a complaint is made against you, a Look Out Circular (LOC) may be issued against you, preventing you from leaving India until court proceedings are finalised. Court proceedings are lengthy, and delays are common, even for minor cases. You may not be informed if an LOC has been placed against you. Most people only know about an LOC when advised by immigration authorities on arrival or departure.
laws.heading: Look Out Circular (LOC)

laws.rule: It's illegal to carry or use satellite phones and satellite-enabled GPS devices without a licence. This includes personal emergency beacons such as Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacons (EPIRBs) or Personal Locator Beacons (PLBs). Australian citizens have been detained and charged with significant fines on entry, exit or during transit, without prior permission from the Indian Department of Telecommunications to carry these devices. Contact the nearest Indian embassy or consulate for advice. If you carry a satellite phone or other satellite-enabled GPS device, you may be imprisoned for up to 3 years, fined up to INR20 million (around USD 233,000), or both. You could also have the devic
laws.heading: Satellite phones and satellite enabled navigation devices

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe and can include mandatory sentences and the death penalty. There is a minimum sentence of 6 months imprisonment for possession of small amounts. A 10-year prison sentence applies for possession of other amounts. The court process is slow, and you could be detained for months or years while your case is processed. The legal drinking age and drinking laws vary across states. The legal drinking age can also vary for different types of alcohol. Some states permit alcohol use for medicinal purposes only. Others require you to hold a permit to buy, transport or drink alcohol. Some states prohibit alcohol from being brought in from outside the state, and polic
laws.heading: Drugs and alcohol

laws.rule: It's illegal to import, carry or use e-cigarettes, vapes or their parts, such as refills. You can be jailed.
laws.heading: E-cigarettes and vaporisers (vapes)

laws.rule: It's illegal to give or receive a dowry. Courts can issue arrest alert notices for dowry claims at the request of one of the parties. If you've been involved in giving or receiving a dowry or a case has been filed against you for dowry and harassment, you could be arrested on arrival in India.
laws.heading: Dowries

laws.rule: Possessing or exporting antiquities without official permission is illegal. For information contact the Indian Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs or an embassy or consulate of India.
laws.heading: Antiquities

laws.rule: It's illegal to photograph or trespass on: airports military establishments dams It's also illegal to take pictures or videos of some places of worship. Always check with the building's administrative office before taking photos or videos.
laws.heading: Photography

laws.rule: It's illegal to: not carry your passport and a valid visa possess firearms or ammunition do religious missionary work without an appropriate visa attempt to convert a person to another religion by force or other enticement In some states, attempting to It's illegal to maim or kill a cow deliberately. The penalty is up to 5 years imprisonment in some states.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Some crimes may result in the death penalty, including: murder kidnapping for ransom armed robbery with murder treason rape, in certain circumstances
laws.heading: Serious crimes

laws.rule: Same sex relationships are legal in India, but same sex marriage is not legally recognised. Indian law doesn't guarantee freedom from discrimination for LGBTQIA+ travellers. Visible displays of same-sex affection can draw unwanted attention.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ travellers

laws.rule: In some areas of India, the Islamic holy month of Ramadan is observed. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws at this time. During Ramadan, eating, drinking and smoking may be illegal in public during the day. If you're not fasting, avoid these activities around people who are. Seek local advice to avoid offending. Read our Ramadan page to learn more, including dates for Ramadan.
laws.heading: Ramadan

laws.rule: You can drive without an Indian driver's licence for 3 months if you have both: an International Driving Permit your current Australian driver's licence (digital driver's licences may not be accepted) Your licence must be valid for the type of vehicle you're driving. You need an Indian driver's licence if you plan to drive for over 3 months. Your insurance may not be valid if you have an accident without the correct licence. You could be liable for the accident as an unlicensed driver.
laws.heading: Driving permit

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Codes of dress and behaviour are strict. These are particularly important at religious sites. Physical contact between men and women in public might be considered inappropriate. Take care not to offend. If in doubt, get local advice. Incredible India: at temples, cover your shoulders and knees and remove footwear. Cover your head at gurdwaras. Some sites ban leather, phones and cameras (for example the Dilwara Jain temples).

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Indian Rupee (INR). ATMs that accept international debit and credit cards are widely available in larger cities and towns. However, they're harder to find in rural areas. Cash shortages at ATMs can be a problem in rural areas. Traveller's cheques are not widely accepted. Counterfeit currency is in circulation. Take care when dealing with cash. - Reserve Bank of India

health-entry.notes: Yellow fever rule as reported to WHO in 2019. WHO advises confirming with the embassy before travel.
conditional: Yellow fever certificate: Anyone (except infants up to the age of 9 months) arriving by air or sea without proof of vaccination against yellow fever is detained in isolation for up to 6 days if that person (i ) arrives within 6 days of departure from an area with risk of yellow fever transmission, or (ii) has been in such an area in transit (except those passengers and members of the crew who, while in transit through an airport situated in an area with risk of yellow fever transmission, remained within the airport premises during the period of their entire stay and the Health Officer agrees to such exemption), or (iii) arrives on a ship that started from or touched at any port in an area with risk of yellow fev er transmission up to 30 days before its arrival in India, unless such a ship has been disinsected in accordance with the procedure laid down by WHO, or (iv) arrives on an aircraft that has been in an area with risk of yellow fever transmission and has not been disinsected in accordance with the Indian Aircraft Public Health Rules, 1954, or as recommended by WHO. Countries and areas regarded as having risk of yellow fever transmission are, in Africa: Angola, Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, Côte dʼIvoire, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, Sierra Leone, South Sudan, Sudan, Togo and Uganda; and in the Americas: Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago (Trinidad only) and Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of). Note: When a case of yellow fever is re ported from any country, that country is regarded by the Government of India as a country with risk of yellow fever transmission and is added to the above list

Proof of oral polio vaccination at least 4 weeks before departure for resident national travellers from polio - endemic countries (Afghanistan, Nigeria, Pakistan) and countries with poliovirus circulation following importation (Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Syrian Arab Republic) is required
